issues.description: The problem statement uses a snake_case method name 'get_total_number_of_students()' while the UML, template comments, and the solution implementation use the camelCase name 'getTotalNumberOfStudents()'. This mismatch between the textual requirement and the code-level identifiers can confuse students about the exact method they should implement and increase extraneous cognitive load when mapping the task description to Java code (which conventionally uses camelCase).
issues.suggestedFix: Unify the identifier naming. Update problem_statement.md to refer to getTotalNumberOfStudents() (camelCase) to match the UML and Java conventions used in the template and solution. Alternatively, if the snake_case form was intentional, update the template/tests/solution to match it—however, prefer camelCase to follow Java conventions.
